patches.title: [Wave 3] Star Citizen Alpha 5.0 PTU Patch Notes 13248297

n: Alpha Patch 5.0 has been released and is now available to test on the PTU environment! Patch should now show: VERSION 5.0.0-PTU.13248297
Server Info: PTU Channel - US Only
25x Rep reward multiplier is currently active on PTU
Stability, Bugfixes, LTP between PTU releases

Two new location types have been added to Nyx I this build: extraction hubs and medium settlements, which should broaden the range of places you come across while exploring. The landing pads have had a lighting pass covering offset lights, stair and railing decals and a clipping lamp post, and surveillance towers have had their night-time lighting improved, with the rotating lights moved onto the tower itself so they track properly.
The Forager’s Guide has been updated for Nyx I
Potential Fix: Missing or broken ledges on storage, watchtower, compound and maintenance tiles
Potential Fix: Inverted and misaligned cover barrier collisions, railing issues, and incorrect tints across compound tiles in 80m guild halls
Potential Fix: Non-usable chairs and stools replaced with usable versions
Potential Fix: Terrain modifier settings around turrets causing noisy terrain
Remote contract locations now read as “Unoccupied Territory” rather than a blank address
Potential Fix: Eliminate Boss contracts failing on the Vaughn target (
Potential Fix: Notice board courier contracts failing to generate
Potential Fix: Courier delivery targets being miscounted, with deliveries now distributed correctly across multiple buildings at a location
Potential Fix: ASD Delving deliveries not using the freight elevator

Lightning has been substantially reworked. Strike frequency and interval are now driven by actual cloud coverage and lightning strength from the weather system rather than a fixed random rate, with coverage mapped across a grid so a fully overcast sky behaves differently from patchy cloud. Separate paths now handle lightning spawned by a shape and lightning generated around the camera, and only one strike at a time can drive the volumetric cloud lighting.
Creatures and harvestables now spawn in the correct zone
Reduced VRAM use and further terrain shader optimization
Water surface and caustics now render correctly at distance from the zone origin
Cloud and coverage lighting settings corrected

Biome ambience has had a wide set of improvements this build, with a mix pass and content tweaks to bring what you hear in line with what you are looking at. Weather audio has been expanded considerably with cold winds and sandstorms added alongside improved rain content, and there is a first pass at rain occlusion so smaller buildings now offer some shelter from the sound. Rain is also now audible from inside ship interiors, so sitting out a storm on the surface should feel far less silent than before.
Improved rain content, with first pass rain occlusion for smaller buildings
Rain now audible from inside ship interiors
Planetary audio now fades out by altitude as you climb, rather than carrying ground ambience into the sky
Tree ambience reworked to prevent phasing where overlapping sounds cancelled one another

Footsteps have had a full mix pass, and the weapon mix pass continues with more weapons brought in line each build. Explosions on Starchitect tiles have seen many improvements, with further work still to come.

Ambience and interaction design across the Starchitect tiles has had significant work this build, along with a mix pass. Guild halls now have ambient computer and lighting audio, and powerable surveillance towers and satellites give proper audio feedback as they come online.
VOIP has had substantial reliability and networking work on the service side this cycle, aimed at how consistently voice connects and holds up during play.

Alongside that, two long-standing voice problems have been addressed. Releasing push to talk no longer cuts off your final words, since the game now waits briefly before muting rather than discarding audio still arriving from your microphone. Separately, hearing a party member’s speech repeat itself seconds or even minutes later has been fixed; the game was holding an unplayed second copy of nearby party speech and playing that back when you moved far enough away to switch channels.

Audio may stutter, crackle or pop during play. Vegetation interaction sounds are still being worked on, hangars are currently missing their ambience, and the mix at the Nyx stations needs further work.

Beach and swamp biome ambience still has issues to be tweaked and fixed. Some of the new Nyx biomes report the wrong surface underfoot, so grass may sound like gravel, rock or sand. A number of weapons have yet to go through the mix pass. And when several mining lasers are operating close together, the combined audio becomes extremely loud.
The Personal Inner Thought, Personal Inner Space, and quick access wheels now render as 3D objects, with selection by head or eye gaze, plus new options for wheel placement and scale
AR marker limits raised in VR so distant markers no longer disappear early due to the wider field of view
As a temporary fix we have disabled the Ursa Medivac alarm sound that was causing endless loops
Potential Fix: Missiles doing no damage to ships with interiors, with hull hits now resolving in the correct zone (
Potential Fix: Ships failing to stow when the player left the landing area while the ship was on the pad of an instanced hangar (
Potential Fix: Thruster audio looping indefinitely when a ship switched between player and non-player audio models
Potential Fix: Players and NPCs falling through the floor when walking slowly out of a guild hall interior
Potential Fix: Pirate Swarm wave 10 never completing when the player chose the Idris-M
Potential Fix: Missing room system in the Lorville CBD stairwell
Potential Fix: Accept and decline prompts displaying as a percentage meter rather than showing their options
Potential Fix: A series of GPU crashes affecting both the Persistent Universe and Arena Commander, covering the planet texture bake, fog shader, and fallback textures (
Potential Fix: Client hang while planet assets were loading
Potential Fix: Server deadlock between the component scheduler and entity hierarchy locks
Potential Fix: Fatal error caused by the Drake Cutter’s rear landing gear

Exterior lighting has had a polish and optimization pass across all tile types, and interior dressing continues through habitation and command buildings.

patches.title: [Wave 3] Star Citizen Alpha 5.0 PTU Patch Notes 13228337

n: Alpha Patch 5.0 has been released and is now available to test on the PTU environment! Patch should now show: VERSION 5.0.0-PTU.13228337
Server Info: PTU Channel - US Only
Stability, Bugfixes, LTP between PTU releases

Contract scope now has a full visual language in the interface. Each contract carries an icon and color indicating whether it is local, planetary, system-wide or universal, so you can tell at a glance how far a job will take you before you accept it. Hauling objectives have also been improved, with markers now pointing at the nearest valid freight elevator kiosk once you arrive at a pickup or drop-off rather than leaving you to find it yourself. Resource gathering quantities on notice boards have been rebalanced alongside this.
Potential Fix: Notice board contracts failing to generate
Potential Fix: Objective display on multi-to-single courier contracts
Potential Fix: Contract generation failing when searching for locations across multiple shards (

Potential Fix: Refuelling contracts not completing after the location streamed back in
The track button now works both ways. Pressing it on a contract that is already tracked will untrack it, rather than doing nothing.

Traversal and navigation work continues, with ledge markup now extended across guild halls and every landing pad size, and unnecessary climbing points removed from cluttered desks and similar surfaces where they were never intended. Navigation passes have gone through the compound tiles, and the spawn closet doors in maintenance buildings no longer trap AI trying to get through them.

A new lighting flare library has been rolled out across exterior tiles this build, covering watchtowers, extraction sets, command buildings and logistics exteriors. Compound and habitation interiors have had further lighting and dressing passes.

Potential Fix: Bars over roof glass that players could snag on
Potential Fix: Salvage vents not presenting their salvageable material
Potential Fix: Oversized landing particle effects beneath some ships
Potential Fix: NPCs spawning beneath the terrain at Nyx Social Station

Reeds have been added to Nyx I with updated distribution settings, and scattered rocks now use their proper biome accumulation group, so snow and surface material build up on them as they do on the terrain around them. Rain and lightning have both had further polish passes, and cloud coverage settings have been adjusted to address atmospheric lighting reading too dark under overcast conditions.
Water areas are now mirrored correctly into surrogate physics grids and kept in sync as those areas change
Potential Fix: Vertex shimmer and fizzling on scattered instances
Potential Fix: Temporal anti-aliasing incorrectly handling fast-moving detail

Ships can now be heard taking off and landing from outside the vehicle, with the audio varying by hull size across small, medium, large and capital classes. This sits alongside the existing pass-by and movement audio, so a ship departing a pad near you should now read as an event rather than passing in silence. Audio propagation has also been reworked for ships heard from inside buildings, and faction announcements now play across compound tannoy systems.
Potential Fix: The Hammerhead failing to spawn on wave 8 of Pirate Swarm, making the mode impossible to complete
Potential Fix: The extra life awarded after clearing wave 4 of Pirate Swarm not letting players who had already used all their lives respawn

Potential Fix: NPCs dying at random to collision from unknown sources when attempting to use interactables
Potential Fix: Cockpit and interior components on several ships being incorrectly treated as non-insurable, which prevented those ships from being created correctly
The server stability work continues, with four dedicated game server crashes addressed this build alongside a longstanding client crash affecting both the PU and AC.
Potential Fix: Server crash caused by an entity being linked to the same area twice
Potential Fix: Server crash when naming a surrogate manager physics entity
Potential Fix: Server crash retrieving component parameters

patches.title: [Wave 1] Star Citizen Alpha 5.0 PTU Patch Notes 13215521

n: Alpha Patch 5.0 has been released and is now available to test on the PTU environment! Patch should now show: VERSION 5.0.0-PTU.13215521
Server Info: PTU Channel - US Only
Stability, Bugfixes, LTP between PTU releases
Reputation and reward setup is now complete across the remaining guilds operating on Nyx I. The notice board artwork and tooltip layout have been finalized alongside this.
Potential Fix: Some Interstellar Transport Guild contracts being impossible to find on any mission board despite existing in the world
Potential Fix: Notice board courier contracts and their follow-ups failing to generate because a mission item was missing
Potential Fix: Resource gathering contracts completing without awarding their rewards

The main focus this build has been traversal. Ledge markup now covers the remaining tile types across depot, campsite, habitation, logistics and surveillance, so climbing routes should behave consistently wherever you find them, and a broad pass has gone through props, chairs and AI placement to remove the spots where players were getting stuck. New lighting flares around locations have been introduced and surveillance towers now respond to their own power state, with their lighting tied to whether the tower is running. Those towers can also be brought back online as contract objectives.

Elsewhere, guild halls have had signage, branding, and navigation passes with new signage materials, minimap location labels have been added, set dressing continues through habitation interiors and lobbies and with updated navigation meshes so AI can path around it.
Potential Fix: A section of terrain at one location where players would clip through the surface of the planet (
Potential Fix: An office chair in a guild hall that players were unable to stand up from, and another that threw players through a wall when they left it
Potential Fix: A railing clipping through the left side of the guild hall steps
Potential Fix: Abandoned ships accumulating at locations across Nyx I, which were receiving little to no cleanup

Biome transitions and species dominance have been re-tuned across the planet, changing how foliage shifts and which plants hold ground in each region. Rain ripple strength has been reduced on wet surfaces, which had been reading too strongly, and there is further work on water and wetting visuals generally. Terrain rendering has also been optimized, including skipping tessellation entirely on distant terrain.

One notable change for anyone flying the system: the Nyx I Lagrange point has been moved. The old position left the planet poorly lit from Delta Station with the sun directly overhead, so it now sits where the planet reads better from the station.
Potential Fix: Lighting missing from the extractor

The temporary fix applied to Tactical Strike Group interactions has been replaced with a full implementation. The Assist Ship In Combat contract has been temporarily disabled, as recent combat balance changes left it unwinnable rather than merely difficult; it will return once the balance settles.
Potential Fix: Tactical Strike Group interaction reset (

The territory configuration format has been updated with a robustness pass over how territory boxes and grids are loaded. The replication layer now batches entity removal commands rather than issuing them individually, splitting the batch above a configurable limit.
Potential Fix: Remote turret self status MFD not displaying (
Potential Fix: Squashed buttons on the Mirai Guardian configuration MFD
Potential Fix: The Xanthule flight suit and its variants incorrectly describing backpack compatibility (

A substantial server stability pass has been done for today's build. Three of these were causing dedicated game server crashes or memory exhaustion, including a leak where physics fences were never released when an entity was deleted, which grew for the lifetime of every server.
Potential Fix: Server crash when building collision proxies across multiple threads
Potential Fix: Client and server crash from cross-entity writes during parallel area processing
Potential Fix: Server memory exhaustion from physics fences never being released on entity deletion
Potential Fix: Server crash retrieving a physics controller
Potential Fix: Client crash in the user interface when attaching to a freed node
Potential Fix: Client crash during texture defragmentation
Potential Fix: Client buffer overrun crash (

Additional diagnostics added to Vulkan crash reports covering shader cache state and processor details

patches.title: [Wave 1] Star Citizen Alpha 5.0 PTU Patch Notes 13201184

n: Alpha Patch 5.0 has been released and is now available to test on the PTU environment! Patch should now show: VERSION 5.0.0-PTU.13201184
Server Info: PTU Channel - US Only
Stability, Bugfixes, LTP between PTU releases
TTK (Not a 5.0 feature but in the PTU for the weekend for testing and feedback)

Armor, clothing and magazines have had a complete pass on how much room they occupy in your inventory. These previously used measured physical volume, so a full armour set would not fit in a backpack and a handful of magazines filled your torso. Volume is now assigned by category and usefulness, with magazines tiered by weapon class from pistol at the smallest through to HMG at the largest.

Full armor sets now fit in backpacks, with light, medium, heavy, environment and super heavy all retuned. Environment suits fit a Combat Medium backpack and the BUL-H4 super heavy suit fits a Combat Heavy

Shirts, trousers, jackets and gloves now compress enough to fit in any armor, undersuit or flight suit pocket, with footwear fitting backpacks. Every clothing item now has a defined size, where shirts, gloves, shoes and hats previously had none
Flight suits and racing suits now occupy the same room as undersuits
Light combat and utility backpacks now fit rifles, shotguns, SMGs, the GP-33 and the Novian Crossbow

Theater mode has been rebuilt as a virtual cinema rather than a flat panel floating in front of you. The screen is now curved and sits in a room that it lights, with a selection of environments to watch from, and it can present the game image in stereoscopic 3D using scene depth. Theater mode is now always active in the frontend.
Screen size presets covering Monitor, Living Room, Cinema and Giant Screen, with adjustable curvature and height
Screen Follows Me option keeps the screen in front of you as you turn
Environments: Black, Stars, Aurora, Day and Night, Underwater, Orbit and Storm
3D image option shifts the picture per eye based on scene depth
Screen glow lights the floor and surrounding room
Your monitor can mirror the headset view of the theater
Options menu rebuilt around the new settings, replacing the old scale and distance sliders

Potential Fix: The view pitching when a standing player turned their head on a planet with wind

Potential Fix: Attack on All Fronts objectives not being set up correctly
Loot distribution and interior dressing continue across the generated locations, with a pass on how hostile AI read to players and further work on spawn closets.
Commodities added to extraction tiles, repair loot boxes added to maintenance interiors, and a loot pass across habitation interiors
New doorless spawn closet added to maintenance buildings, allowing interior to exterior transitions, with extraction tile AI now spawning from it
Delivery drop-off points added to the 120m landing pad, with props repositioned near drop-off points to improve navigation
Security locations renamed from a new list
Static screens and empty monitors replaced with working prefabs
Engineers now receive their multitool and tablet through their loadout bundle

Interior kit, command kit and bridge glass work, with lighting and dressing passes across maintenance, logistics and habitation interiors

The main change this build is to how neighbouring terrain patches agree with one another. Patches previously placed and elected their ground cells from their own data, which produced a straight crack along the border with unrelated ground textures on either side. Patches now elect each ground cell at its world centre, so every patch holding that cell agrees on it.

n: Alpha Patch 5.0 has been released and is now available to test on the PTU environment! Patch should now show: VERSION 5.0.0-PTU.13189690
Server Info: PTU Channel - US Only
Stability, Bugfixes, LTP between PTU releases
TTK (Not a 5.0 feature but in the PTU for the weekend for testing and feedback)

The generated locations across Nyx I have had a broad pass covering AI placement, traversal and loot. The largest change is that AI now spawn inside buildings rather than outdoors, which should make encounters read more clearly and stop defenders appearing from open ground. Ledge markup has also been extended across most tile types so climbing routes work consistently.
AI spawn closets moved from exteriors into building interiors across compounds, logistics, habitation, agriculture and depot tiles
Civilians now populate campsites rather than logistics workers, and AI counts reduced in depot and storage tiles

Work on Nyx I this cycle concentrated on the variety and density of surface vegetation, and on the shading of rock and bedrock. A new orange-tinted grass has been added with its own distribution to break up the planet’s palette, and foliage density has been reduced in forest and swamp regions to improve performance.
New grass added with an orange tint and a different distribution, with forest and swamp density reduced
Tree temperature distribution and density updated, and new mineable rock variants added
Reduced VRAM use across planet scattering, and terrain level of detail rebalanced at cube edges
Water simulation updates and imposter wind bending
Potential Fix: Lighting artifacts on vegetation when lit by ship lights
Potential Fix: Harvestables not working consistently, and harvestable node refreshes

Weather on Nyx I has been tuned for frequency and readability, with lightning reworked so strikes are less visually overwhelming while remaining visible at distance. Thunder is now audible, and a new orchestral score has been recorded and mixed for the planet.
Rain frequency increased, with cloud shaping and climate maps split and cloud tuning applied
Lightning light intensity and spawn frequency reduced, with improved falloff
Thunder now audible with managed audio distance increased to 25km, and rain events added with a thunder sound pass

Player footsteps mix pass and fixes. Footsteps should be more consistent.
Improvements to interior/exterior transitions in Starchitect locations

Territory generation, which decides how the world is divided between servers in the mesh, has had substantial work this cycle. Territories now capture an entity’s full transform rather than its position alone, and planets and moons are identified from their own component data rather than inferred.
Claim reservation bias now estimated from entity count
Runtime territory candidates now only considered when explicitly enabled in configuration

Note: We have worked on and are testing a new multiplier system for PTU builds. Tonight's build has a 10x multiplier in for reputation gains to go along with testing on PTU.

Guild reputation has had its initial setup pass, with reward and rank structures built out across several of the employers operating on Nyx I. Contracts now carry a scope, which determines how widely they range, and this is surfaced in both the Contract Manager and on mission boards.

The missile lock interface has been replaced with the version built for Squadron 42. The previous display drew an animated pattern around your target that tightened as the lock built, which told you how far along the lock was but nothing else. The new interface shows the locking cone itself in the centre of the screen, so you can see the area a target has to be inside before a missile will acquire a lock, and it tracks target range on a bar alongside it.
Locking cone displayed in the centre of the screen, with fade in and out
Lock progression now shown as four distinct states: idle, acquiring, locked and resolved
“LOCK” now appears beside the target marker the moment a full lock is achieved

The interface now takes the colour of your ship’s manufacturer HUD styling

patches.title: Star Citizen Alpha 4.10.3 LIVE Release Notes

n: Star Citizen Alpha 4.10.3 has been released onto the LIVE environment!
Your launcher should now display: VERSION 4.10.3-LIVE.13165946
Reminder. Citizens always imprint their ship loadouts before adventuring into the universe!
The RSI Galaxy is a large multi-crew ship built around a swappable central module allowing players to swap out roles when needed.
The Cargo Module takes the Galaxy from its base 64 SCU up to 720 SCU and adds an industrial grade lift, along with tractor beam consoles for loading and unloading.
The Med Bay Module turns the bay into a field hospital with Tier 1, 2, and 3 medbeds..

The Liberator is a heavy carrier for ships and ground vehicles. Ground vehicles load through the rear ramp into the vehicle bay, while ships either fit inside the interior hangar or set down on the landing pads, some within the hull and some along the upper exterior. Anything parked inside the Liberator can use landing services for repair, rearm, and refuel.

The Carrack, Perseus, Starlancer, Starlancer TAC, Hammerhead and Tiburon now carry Size 3 radars in place of Size 2, with their default loadouts updated to match. The component bays housing them have been reworked to fit the larger units, which has moved the Perseus relay onto a console and relocated the Starlancer radar into engineering.
A number of already flyable ships can now be bought in game for the first time with aUEC.
The Aegis Tiburon and MISC Starlite are stocked at New Deal in Lorville,
The Drake Ironclad, Drake Pitbull and MISC Starlite at Teach's Ship Shop on Levski,
The Drake Ironclad Assault, Drake Pitbull, and Grey's Market Basher can now be purchased in Rundown Station in Pyro
The Origin M80 and Gatac Tyilui can now be purchased in Astro Armada in Area18.
The Esperia Prowler Utility's pilot and copilot dashboards have a new interaction that opens the cargo bay doors on their own, without dropping the rear ramp
Ship HUD holograms are now tinted to match the manufacturer of the vehicle

Hull munching capacity has been increased across the salvage fleet: Reclaimer from 240 to 448 SCU, Argo MOTH from 64 to 240 SCU, Vulture from 13 to 16 SCU, MISC Fortune from 13 to 14 SCU and RSI Salvation from 6 to 8 SCU
The disintegration field on all five has been enlarged, with a more forgiving falloff on alignment, so holding a cut on a hull is less exacting
Vanduul AI ships now carry greater ammunition capacity and regenerate ammunition faster, making them markedly more aggressive in sustained fights
The Mauler's weapons have been made considerably more deadly
The Mauler's health has been reduced to balance against its increased firepower
High Risk Target bounty contracts now award 4,000 Bounty Hunters Guild reputation rather than 2,000, placing them correctly between Medium Risk and Very Hard contracts
The minimum arming distance on Size 5 and Size 7 torpedoes has been raised to 700m
For a comprehensive up to date list of Known issues and Workarounds, please check out our Knowledge Base here!
This release closes 13 crash and stability issues.
Fixed a server deadlock on the main thread while an entity was being detached and queued for deletion
Resolved a server crash while a player's mission log was being read
Fixed a server crash in the mission refund path caused by a division by zero
Addressed a server memory leak where a mission queue fed by interactable objects grew without limit
Fixed a client crash in the particle system while effects were being updated
Resolved a client crash while the game was checking the shape of a world object against its bounding volume
Fixed a client crash while converting a vehicle component record to a more specific type that did not match
Fixed a client crash while freeing memory
Resolved a client crash when using two tractor beams at once on a Vulture
Fixed a client crash while streaming a texture that was being rendered to at the same time
Resolved a client crash while building the list of objects a physics query should ignore
Corrected a fatal error raised when a ship registered two parts under the same identifier

Alpha 4.10.3 closes 129 issues, including multiple exploits. Outside the new content the focus is on the things you touch every session: ASOP terminals and hangars, cargo and contracts, freight elevators, and the vehicle HUD.

36 of these came to us through the Issue Council, and each one carries a link to the original report. Where the cause is worth knowing, the fix carries a short note under it explaining what was going wrong and what changed. Reports filed on the Issue Council, along with the confirmations and repro steps added to existing ones, are what let us reproduce an issue reliably and rank it against everything else. Thank you to everyone who takes the time to do it.

A large concentrated pass on the hangar and fleet management loop has been done for 4.10.3. This covers 14 fixes directly related to Hangar and ASOP flow, eight of them raised through the Issue Council.
Fixed an issue where the Retrieve button on an ASOP terminal could become greyed out, leaving you unable to retrieve, store or deliver the selected vehicle

The hangar platform tracks its own position by listening for door events, and if one of those events was lost it sat in a moving state forever, which kept you on the controller's changing ships list and locked the terminal. The platform now checks itself against the doors, replays the missing event, and releases any pending store or retrieve if it cannot.
Corrected an issue where many vehicles showed placeholder text for their status in the Fleet Manager and on ASOP terminals and could not be selected

The vehicle list unloads rows as they scroll out of view, and a row returning to view still held the cached values from before it was unloaded, which is what surfaced as placeholder text in the status, cargo and crew fields; that cache is now cleared.
Fixed a case where a ship left on an instanced hangar pad would not be stowed when the player left the landing location

Stowing a hangar also stows whatever is sitting on the pad, but that nested request left out the piece of configuration that lets your location storage be created on demand, so it failed for anyone who had never stored anything there; it now includes it.
Fixed an issue where impounded ships and the option to pay off their impound fine were not shown on ASOP terminals

The terminal's impound check returned false even for impounded vehicles, so the entry appeared with the ordinary claim option and the fine never showed; that state is now reported correctly and the fine can be paid.
Fixed an issue where retrieving a ground vehicle could cause it to be destroyed on the hangar pad

Releasing a vehicle from the hangar lift could leave it displaced from its set-down spot, or give it enormous velocity on a stationary pad, driving it through the platform; a guard now restores the release pose and stops it dead.
Corrected an issue where ships retrieved from an ASOP terminal lobby could clip into the hangar loading platform

A retrieved ship was placed onto the hangar platform while it was still lowered and did not rise with it, so it ended up embedded in the pad, mostly on the first retrieval of a session; placement has been corrected.
Corrected an issue where the MISC Prospector could be tilted over to one side when retrieved in a hangar

The landing gear hardpoints sat at different heights, so one leg met the pad before the others and the hull settled at an angle, most often in the smallest hangars; the layout has been corrected so every leg sits level.
Resolved an issue where a rented ground vehicle that had been scrapped or destroyed could not be claimed again

Ground vehicles and power suits were not listed in the global item recovery rules that decide what can be insured and reclaimed, which covered spaceships only; both have been added, so an Ursa or an ATLS now behaves like a ship when you claim it.
Fixed an issue where engine effects were already running on some vehicles as soon as they were retrieved

Switching a ship's power on also switched on its engines, which was never intended, so a ship stored while powered came back with engines already running; engine activation is now separate and happens when you set the ship flight ready.
Fixed an issue where hangars could visually overlap, letting players see into neighbouring hangars and the vehicles in them

Spawning into your own hangar skipped the step that limits who the interior streams to, and left the door registered as an open doorway between zones while it was shut, so other instances at that gateway stayed visible; both are now set on spawn.
Fixed a second case where players could see other players' vehicles from inside their own instanced hangar
Resolved an issue where opening an ASOP terminal froze the game for several seconds

The terminal built interface elements for every vehicle you own at once instead of only the rows on screen, over ten thousand of them on a large fleet, stalling rendering for several seconds; only the visible rows are built now.
Resolved an issue where dialogue and sound effects were missing when interacting with the ASOP terminal inside a personal hangar
Corrected an issue where hangars in landing zones added excessive reverb and echo to personal weapon sounds
Fixed an issue where using autoland did not complete the landing objective in the third part of the new player tutorial

The objective never completed after autoland because it checked whether you were registered in the station's action area, which autoland did not satisfy, so it now tests whether the player is inside the landing location itself.
Resolved an issue where a Nyx story mission could not progress past the objective to travel to the Blinding Hope because the ship failed to spawn
The search for the vessel to place at the rendezvous filtered on a content tag that did not exist in this build, so nothing matched and the ship was never created; that filter has been removed.
Fixed a case where the pick-up marker for delivery missions at Levski was placed inside the asteroid

When no suitable container could be resolved, the system fell back to any container under that location, including instanced interiors with no real world position, which at Levski put the marker inside the asteroid. That fallback has been removed.
Fixed an issue where a cargo loading area could stay permanently occupied and block every ship that used it afterwards

A loading area records the vehicle using it, and if that pilot left the game before the transfer finished the record was never cleared, so the area stayed occupied and refused later ships; those stale records are now cleared.
Resolved an issue where the Collector intro mission could not be found in the contract manager
Fixed an issue where accepting a mission card at Wikelo's would also accept other contracts at random

The lookup behind accepting a mission card can return contracts beyond the one it asked for, and the old code accepted every result it was handed rather than just the one you picked; only the contract matching your request is accepted now.
Corrected an issue where the progress counter for a Battaglia story objective stayed at zero after every hostile aboard the Blinding Hope had been killed

The mission builds its hostile count by searching the boarded ship for enemies matching a target description, and this contract never supplied one, so nobody aboard was ever registered; that description is now set and the hostile ship spawn options have been corrected alongside it.
Fixed a case where the vehicle to be salvaged for a Battaglia medium salvage contract would not spawn

The fault was in the vehicle data rather than the contract: the Prospector template and the salvageable Prospector variant both carried incorrect tags, and both have been retagged so the right ship is placed at the site.
Fixed an issue where mission objective text was cut short on the player HUD
Fixed an issue where ships spawned into a mission area at partial health would climb back to full shortly afterwards

Spawning a ship with preset damage only translated that figure into actual damage for entities that track individual hit locations, and ships were not covered by that check, so nothing was ever really damaged; vehicles now run through the same path.
Fixed an issue where hostile ships in Bounty Hunter and Mercenary missions would sometimes not return fire

After finishing an intercept run, hostile pilots did not reliably return to standard combat flight mode, and in that state they would close with you but never fire, so the behaviour now switches back explicitly when the intercept completes.
Resolved an issue where a large amount of extra cargo would appear in the freight elevator after completing a Recover Cargo contract

Hand-in progress counted each container's volume rather than the container itself, so a few boxes registered as far more than you delivered and the surplus came back as a refund; progress now counts each container as one item.
Resolved an issue where the contract list in the mobiGlas could become stuck and would not scroll through the available contracts

The offer list had no interaction target of its own and the contract cards sat in front of it, so the mouse wheel was captured by the cards; the list now has its own target and sits nearer the camera.
Fixed a case where there was no prompt to place an item into the dumbwaiter during an IASI mission

The drop-off point on those lockers was exported at the model's origin rather than where it had been placed, so in game it sat buried inside the unit where nothing could reach it even though the setup looked right; the animations have been re-exported.
Corrected an issue where only one player could hold a given PVP bounty contract at a time
Fixed an issue where the augmented reality marker for a mission location would disappear once the player was around 3km from the destination
Fixed a case where Gilly would not be present to greet the player after accepting the first Combat Gauntlet mission
Resolved an issue where some mission descriptions told players to travel to a derelict outpost while the objective was actually inside an underground bunker
Fixed an issue where placeholder spheres appeared in place of the weapon racks aboard some ships

The racks sit inside prebuilt room containers on the affected ships rather than being assembled as the ship loads, and those containers had to be exported again for this release before the racks would come through with the rest of the room.
Corrected an issue where the Drake Caterpillar's power plant could only be repaired from one narrow angle

Collision belonging to the railing below the power plant extended up around the component itself, leaving only one narrow angle from which a tool or weapon could actually reach it; the collision in that corner has been reworked.
Resolved an issue where players could get stuck on the power plant railings aboard the Drake Caterpillar, encountered during a Battaglia story mission

Collision around the railings left a corner a character could step into and not get back out of; a barrier that only players collide with now seals it off, and the engine room's collision shapes were reworked in the same pass.
Fixed a problem where landing gear springs provided no stiffness on vehicles with unusual leg layouts

Load balancing across the legs measured each one along a fixed ship axis and pushed them all along a single averaged direction, so rotated or unevenly spaced legs received almost no force whatever their stiffness; each leg now uses its own orientation and spacing.
Resolved an issue where ship components all used the same distortion resistance value instead of one appropriate to their size

Several components, including the event reward coolers, power plants and radars, were left on a placeholder distortion resistance of ten, far weaker than their size allows, so ships fitted with them went offline almost immediately; correct values are now set.
Fixed a problem where ships could skip being disabled and be destroyed outright when taking sustained continuous fire

The extra health buffer that should leave a ship disabled rather than destroyed was not being drawn on under one unbroken stream of fire, so ships went straight from intact to wreckage; the destruction path now consumes it properly.
Fixed an issue where landing services requested through the mobiGlas could become stuck showing a processing or blocked prompt

When the server had no authority over your wallet, a mobiGlas purchase failed before the request was recorded as pending, so the shop was never told and the stale entry blocked later requests; the request is now recorded first.
Fixed an issue where a vehicle that had been vented to a planet's atmosphere would not correctly restore its internal atmosphere, leaving players inside to suffocate or take damage from the cold

A vehicle vented on a cold planet refills with gas at the outside temperature, and life support reheated it far more slowly than it added warm gas, so occupants suffocated or took cold damage; those values have been rebalanced.
Fixed a problem where a ship's life support could report a level far above 100 percent

The engineering readout compares life support's load with its rating, and reheating cold gas cost far more than adding warm gas, so the system was driven past that rating and reported up to 200 percent; the values have been rebalanced.
Fixed an issue where players were unable to change the default power distribution on a vehicle

Every ship started with the same fixed power distribution, so vehicles carrying tractor beams, mining lasers or salvage heads powered up with those systems off and players had to redistribute pips themselves; defaults have been reset fleetwide.
Fixed an issue where the Esperia Prowler Utility was missing its cockpit controller, leaving the pilot unable to use ship systems

The data file defining the ship's cockpit dashboard was never added to the build's asset inclusion list, so it did not ship with the vehicle and the cockpit had no controls to load; that file is now included.
Fixed a case where the vehicle HUD would display as placeholder or dark grey textures

The material that the vehicle augmented reality interface draws itself with was missing from the build's asset inclusion list, so the game had nothing to load for it and fell back to its placeholder texture; the material is now included.
Corrected an issue where the aiming pip on the IFR-BC7 turret would lag behind moving targets while gimbals were enabled

The turret's gimbal mount was built without the yaw and pitch pivots the aiming system drives, so the guns never swivelled even though gimbal mode engaged, and only moving targets revealed it; those pivots have been added.
Resolved an issue where the targeting pip would vanish when a turret was aimed high

The material drawing the turret's targeting shapes faded them out almost completely once they were viewed at a sharp angle; those elements now use a material that stays visible across a much wider range of viewing angles.
Fixed a case where Stalker V CS missiles tracked so strongly that they could not be thrown off with countermeasures once they had locked on
Resolved an issue where a ship with a destroyed power plant could not be salvaged because it was still reported as powered on

The structural salvage check asked whether any power plant was switched on rather than whether it was still functional, so a plant that had been destroyed but was still flagged as online kept counting; the check now tests for a working plant.
Fixed an issue where the VTOL thrusters on the Esperia Prowler Utility did not rotate into position when VTOL was activated

The VTOL thruster movement on this variant was driven by animation data that had not been exported correctly, so the nozzles stayed parked whatever the flight system asked for; the landing gear and VTOL animations have been re-exported and corrected.
Resolved an issue where docking a snub to its host ship could produce a grinding sound

The docking sound had no cap on how many copies of it could play at once, so repeated triggers stacked overlapping instances on top of each other; a voice limit has now been added so only a controlled number play together.
Fixed a case where the Constellation Phoenix elevator pistons clipped through the lift

The Invictus paint scheme carried a redundant duplicate of the lift geometry, which meant applying that livery made the elevator swap over to the duplicate parts; the extra geometry has been removed from the paint.
Corrected an issue where the lamp on the RSI Skylark was absent

Two settings on the Skylark's material, refraction and light amplification, had been left switched off, which left the effect with nothing to render through; both have been re-enabled on the material.
Resolved an issue where the Esperia Prowler Utility's configuration tab showed a raw text label instead of a name

The attached part item category had never been given a display name of its own in the text library, so anything of that type fell through to showing its raw internal label; a proper name has been added and linked to the category.
Fixed an issue where a wall in the cargo bay of the RSI Zeus Mk II ES would flicker or drop out depending on the angle it was viewed from

The visibility volume covering the neighbouring corridor and the portal leading off it sat slightly too low against the surrounding geometry, which left the cargo bay wall uncovered from some angles; both have been raised.

Corrected an issue where there was no bed logout point in the left room of the recreation area on the Constellation Phoenix, and where the right bed could be used for logout without the usual restrictions
Fixed a case where the player would inconsistently lean forwards after entering the lower turret on Constellation Gold Standard variants
Resolved an issue where damage mesh clipped into the crew area behind the port bunks on Constellation Gold Standard variants
Fixed an issue where audio for the cargo and personnel elevators on Constellation Gold Standard variants was missing or too quiet
Corrected an issue where the Aegis Idris-P was using the armor intended for the Idris-M
Fixed a problem where the top cover of the Aegis Gladius Dunlevy's fuel port was too glossy and did not match the color of the surrounding hull
Resolved an issue where textures would pop in on the windows of the Anvil Centurion
Fixed an issue where space braking and afterburner audio on the Crusader Intrepid was extremely loud
Corrected an issue where the external personal storage cubby on the RSI Skylark had no sound when closing
Fixed a case where Gatac missiles launched at the wrong angle and clipped through the hull
Resolved an issue where inner thought prompts were displayed sideways and were hard to read in the pilot, copilot and turret seats of Gatac ships
Fixed an issue where operator and display button labels in the pilot seat were cut off and did not fit their frames on the Aegis Redeemer and Gladius
Corrected an issue where the turret weapon highlight circles on the MFD self status page were too large
Fixed a case where multifunction displays washed out in direct sunlight, by adding dynamic brightness
Resolved an issue where the G-Safe annunciator used the same label as the landing gear annunciator
Fixed an issue where the Baler salvage head had no model in the 3D view of the engineering terminal
Corrected an issue where the room control panel in a ship's crew habitation could not open or close its door, though it could still work the lights
Corrected an issue where the Drake Golem played no audio alert while carrying unstable Quantanium
Resolved an issue where the TOAG Laser Repeater S3 made no sound when fired
Fixed an issue where the Size 4 Polaris shield carried the wrong name and description
Fixed an issue where a purchase could fail and time out, blocking all further shop purchases

A purchase was only recorded after the payment request was sent, so an instant rejection ran the failure path before any record existed. The record was then written and never cleared, blocking later purchases; the steps are now reordered.
Fixed an issue where commodity purchases at kiosks would eventually start failing even though there was still space available on the ship's cargo grid

The kiosk's figure for remaining ship capacity was not updated as purchases completed, so after several buys it no longer matched the cargo grid and transactions were refused; capacity is now reported in step with the grid.
Fixed a case where cargo could be lost when a request to remove it from a Freight Elevator failed

Taking cargo back off the elevator ran the mission order cleanup even when the request failed, and that cleanup could take the items with it, so a failed request cost you the cargo; it no longer runs on failure.
Fixed an issue where vehicle modules could be pulled out through a Freight Elevator

Vehicle modules were small enough in inventory terms for freight elevators to accept them, so they could be moved through a system never built to handle them and could be lost outright; module sizes have been increased past that limit.
Fixed an issue where the stats of crafted items stored inside containers did not persist between patches

When a container went into long term storage, the saved data holding a crafted item's rolled stats was attached only to items being moved at that moment, so anything already inside came back with default values; records now cover everything.
Corrected an issue where the crafted TH-01 Propulsor had the wrong item size and took up far too little space in inventory

The crafted version of the component was authored with a volume far smaller than the part it represents, so inventory checks barely counted it and hundreds fitted in one backpack; its size has been corrected.
Corrected an issue where refinery processing methods displayed the wrong description text

Each refining method's description was tied to its position in the list, and that list is not built in the same order every time, so the description rarely matched the method selected; the text now lives with the method's data.
Fixed a problem where inventory kiosks did not always show the full contents of a player's inventory
Fixed an issue where the Yormandi Tongue took up almost no space when stored, despite being a large two handed carryable
Resolved an issue where the name of an item held in a tractor beam was cut short rather than wrapping
Fixed a case where the Store option on the interaction wheel did nothing for item cases
Corrected an issue where prices on the augmented reality shopping cards of displayed items appeared offset or broken from some angles
Fixed an issue where the side stand on the Constellation Phoenix commemorative display disappeared when viewed from certain distances
Resolved an issue where the bottom section of the RSI Venture Executive armor display had no collision
Corrected an issue where no variant of the MaxLift tractor beam or the Cambio SRT could be placed on the Bosco weapon display rack
Fixed an issue where the ship on the Aurora Mk II and RSI Constellation Mk IV Andromeda display models cast no shadow while the stand beneath it did
Fixed a case where the RSI Constellation Mk IV Andromeda model floated in mid air when snapped to a freight elevator or ship cargo grid
Resolved an issue where Monolith helmets would visibly change shading as the camera moved closer or further away, across every variant
Fixed an issue where some undersuits clipped through the arms of the Monolith Runic heavy armor
Corrected an issue where the material around the shoulder and armpit of the Monolith heavy armor looked low resolution and distorted while holding a weapon
Fixed an issue where a stray spinning object could be seen when charging or firing the Arrowhead sniper rifle and its variants
Fixed a case where the heavy helmet from the Orison relief armor sets used incorrect textures
Resolved an issue where the female character's left arm stretched and distorted while holding a long rifle
Corrected an issue where every variant of the Omarof optic carried the same name as the default
Fixed an issue where some utility items were significantly louder than the rest
Fixed a problem where some eyebrow options appeared with a placeholder texture in the character customizer

Several eyebrow options were listed in the customizer, but their materials and meshes were never brought into the 4.10 release, so the game had nothing to load and fell back to a missing asset texture; those assets are now included.
Fixed an issue where a newly added friend did not appear in the friends list and could not be found by searching

The game sent an out of date key when asking the Spectrum service about accounts, so every lookup was rejected; that key has been updated. Because the failure was at the lookup stage, adding someone through Spectrum directly still worked.
Fixed an issue where the names shown for the Venture Starwalker and Infrared suits were swapped with each other
Fixed an issue where players approaching the Area18 starport were given a warning and then despawned

The restricted areas around the city centre and its tower were two large spheres that reached into the spaceport approach, and the warning before despawn was fifteen seconds; they are now smaller merged boxes with a ninety second warning.
Resolved an issue where air traffic control voice lines were not audible to the player

Air traffic control audio plays on the controller's own sound object, which sat kilometers away and so fell outside the range where sound objects are kept alive, and the override meant to force it active never worked; both are fixed.
Fixed an issue where air traffic control could not be contacted to land at or leave Distribution Centers

The affected depots shipped without any air traffic control set up in their final layout, so there was no controller to appear in your comms list or to answer a hail; the missing setup has been added.
Fixed a case where rocks and scattered scenery appeared smeared into streaks

Motion data for rocks and similar scattered scenery was never generated, because the instruction to produce it was being passed into the wrong place in the rendering code, leaving the image reconstruction pass with nothing to track those surfaces by; that is now corrected.
Corrected an issue where a door beside the coffee stand in the Area18 spaceport was missing
Resolved an issue where footsteps did not change to match the surface being walked on, and some foley sounds were missing entirely

Audio objects are recycled, and a recycled one still carried the parameter values cached by its previous owner, so a request to set the surface material to a value that matched that stale cache was discarded as redundant; the cache is now emptied on reuse.
Fixed an issue where some planet surface buildings on ArcCorp had no collision

Between 4.10.2 going live and this release we shipped five hotfix builds to the live environment. Only the first of those included a client update, so most of what follows reached you without a download. Everything here is already in your hands and is listed for completeness rather than as new in 4.10.3.
Fixed a server crash loop that was destabilising shards, caused by character heads spawning an eyebrow with no geometry that was then never cleaned up
Resolved an unhandled exception raised when a zone was deleted before it had finished emptying
Fixed a server crash while a player's mission log was being read at the end of a contract
Resolved a server crash in the mission refund path caused by a division by zero
Fixed a problem where ships could explode on contact with hangar doors, by making the collision damage suppression independent of server frame rate and guarding against ships desyncing inside hangars

Corrected an issue where the Retrieve button on an ASOP terminal could stay greyed out indefinitely, by adding a one minute failsafe that releases a vehicle stuck mid retrieval. The underlying cause is fixed properly in this release
Fixed an issue where reopening an ASOP terminal cleared the vehicle claim timer, and where a delivery time was shown while the delivery system was switched off
Resolved an issue where RSI Discovery Month scores did not add up correctly, because completion points on shared salvage and Quantanium mining contracts were not split between party members
Fixed a case where IASI Courier packages around Hurston spawned deep inside Distribution Centers, where collecting them flagged the player for trespassing
Corrected an issue where the game failed to start on newly released NVidia laptop hardware, and where HDR was offered on displays that could not support it rather than being shown as unavailable

patches.title: Star Citizen Alpha 4.10.2 LIVE Release Notes

n: Star Citizen Alpha 4.10.2 has been released onto the LIVE environment!
Your launcher should now display: VERSION 4.10.2-LIVE.12881860
Reminder. Citizens always imprint their ship loadouts before adventuring into the universe!
Shield resistance values no longer require the minimum to be lower than the maximum, which means resistances set to a flat value now actually apply rather than being ignored
Abandoned vehicles left at Everus Harbor, Seraphim Station, Bajini Point and Port Tressler now expire on their own timer
New: VR now has its own zoom, which works by narrowing the field of view. This is meant to be a temporary solution for scopes until we have fully physicalized Scopes. It's enabled for:
A new Zoom Gameplay Strength option controls how strong the zoom is. Set it lower to reduce the effect, or set it to 0 to turn VR zoom off completely.
Advanced users can use these cvars for a more customized experience:
r_StereoZoomScopeMin (1.0): scopes at or below this magnification don't zoom.
r_StereoZoomHeadTrackingRotationScale (1.0): makes the view turn less than your head while zoomed, to reduce discomfort. 0 turns it off.
r_StereoZoomDisablePositionalTracking (2): limits head movement while zoomed. 0 = normal tracking, 1 = off, 2 = only forward/back.
r_StereoZoomLockAngle (10): how close (in degrees) your head must point to your aim for the zoom to apply.
r_StereoZoomLockReleaseScale (1.5): extra margin before the zoom releases, so it doesn't flicker.
r_StereoZoomScopeAlignDistance (0.04): how close (in meters) your eye must be to the scope's line of sight.
r_StereoZoomSmoothTime (0.2): how many seconds the zoom takes to ease in and out.
Fixed some UI icons disappearing after their spawn animation.
Fixed mouse smoothing and acceleration resetting when switching to VR.
Grounded Look now uses your aim direction for hand mining and similar actions.
In Freelook (Z), you can now aim the tractor beam with your head.
The Heavy Combat Hunter 3 armor set arrives with its full range of tints
Three camouflage variants have been added to the RRS armor line
Nine new eyebrow options have been added to character customisation
Wikelo is now trading recipes for the Gemini LMG and Grey Combat Armour, with a new mission to go with the LMG
An RSI Constellation Mk II promotional display and an RSI branded two handed crate have been added as props
For a comprehensive up to date list of Known issues and Workarounds, please check out our Knowledge Base here!

Alpha 4.10.2 closes 71 issues since 4.10.1 went live, including multiple exploits. These focus on long standing ship and item problems, vehicles going unresponsive coming out of quantum, contracts reporting themselves unavailable the moment you accepted them, landing gear and decals rendering badly across several hulls, armor and helmet sets with wrong names, missing parts or no storage, and vehicles coming out of a hangar tilted or with their engines already running. 13 of those came to us directly through the Issue Council, and each one carries a link to the original report.
This release closes five further crash and stability issues.
Fixed a client crash in the vehicle landing gear system, triggered while it was handling an event from a component that was no longer in a valid state
Resolved a client crash while mission modifiers were being applied to a player's mission log
Fixed a hang in the mission generation service while it was building out the hierarchy of the universe, which could stall contract creation, alongside optimisations to that registration path
Resolved a crash while the game was looking up a component on an object that had already been torn down
Fixed a crash while converting a game data record to a more specific type that did not match
Resolved an issue where Orison Relief Support salvage contracts could be completed far faster than intended, making the reward track trivial to rush

The hand in quantities on these contracts were set far lower than the reward track was balanced around, small enough that the whole progression could be cleared in a handful of very short runs. The required amounts have been raised substantially across the small, medium and large versions, and their difficulty ratings have been updated to match the work now involved.
Fixed an issue where the mission item TH-01 Propulsor was listed under Containers instead of Missions in the fabricator
Fixed an issue where the TH-01 Propulsor fabricator's description had overlapping text in the crafting item preview
Fixed an issue where some comms towers would not spin again after their nodes were reset during Siege of Orison
Fixed a case where the entrance and exit doors of the Command Center airlock could suddenly open during the Siege of Orison boss fight

The encounter runs in stages, and each stage ends when the commander's health drops to a set threshold, which is what repositions him for the next one. The final stage had no next position to move to, but the threshold still counted as the stage completing, so the doors opened and he stopped firing while he was still alive. The final stage now ends on his death instead.
Resolved an issue where handing in all mission cargo at the first delivery point of a multi-stop hauling contract could cause the remaining cargo to disappear

When cargo is sent down on a freight elevator for a hand in, everything on the platform is taken and anything the objective did not need is meant to come straight back as a refund. That refund path was unreliable, so leftover cargo could go missing instead of being returned. Refunds now consistently give back everything that went in and was not consumed by the objective.
Fixed an issue where players were marked as trespassing at Cry-Astro locations while on a legal delivery mission

The pool of locations these delivery contracts could draw from included unlawful sites, so a perfectly legal contract could route you somewhere you had no permission to be. Unlawful locations and distribution centers are now excluded when a contract picks its pickup and drop off points.
Fixed an issue where animal hunting missions could send players to a location with no Kopion or Marok present

Animal hunting contracts are built as sub contracts that inherit their creature list from a parent contract, and that inheritance was not resolving, so the sub contract never learned which animals to place. The lookup has been fixed, so the mission now knows what to spawn at the location it sends you to.
Fixed an issue where the refractor array codes displayed as zeros during the QV Breaker Station Mining Rights missions in Nyx

The screens that show each array's code were displaying a placeholder value rather than the code the mission had generated for that run. They now read the generated code, so what is on the screen is the code the array expects.
Fixed an issue where the salvage objective on Battaglia contracts could reach 0% before most or all of the target ship's hull had been scraped
Fixed a problem where Eliminate Target bounty missions named the wrong vehicle for the assigned target

The ship type in the title was taken from the contract's expected target rather than from the vehicle the target actually turned up in, and those two could differ. Rather than leave a name in there that might be wrong, the ship type has been dropped from Eliminate Target titles altogether.
Fixed an issue where a range of contracts would report themselves as unavailable the moment you accepted them in mobiGlas

The randomized seeding used when generating this family of contracts was interfering with the generation step itself, so the contracts it produced could not actually be taken on even though they appeared in the list. The seeding has been corrected so generation completes properly and accepted contracts stay available.
Fixed an issue where players were missing the holographic skull head in the Arena Commander Kill Collector FPS mode while the Day of the Vara event was active
Corrected an issue where outdated textures could be seen in the reflections on helmet visors in New Babbage

Reflections on surfaces like visors in New Babbage are drawn from a pre-baked snapshot of the surroundings rather than rendered live, and that snapshot still held an earlier version of the location's textures. The snapshot has been regenerated against the current textures, so reflections now match what is actually there.
Corrected an issue where the exterior sections of Distribution Centers had no harvestable resources to collect

The harvestable resource points at Distribution Centers are generated by propagating loot setup out into the location's sub areas, and that step was failing to export for the exterior because of how the area volumes are scaled on a planet surface. The propagation and the underlying export error have both been fixed, so the outdoor sections now receive their harvestable points as intended.
Fixed an issue where the fifth player entering a Siege of Orison instance could be left behind instead of being moved to join the rest of their party

Late arrivals are supposed to be moved across to join the rest of their group, but the check that triggered the move looked at whether the player's data was streaming rather than at whether that machine had authority over the player. With the party owner already in the main instance, the fifth player's request was evaluated in the wrong place and never acted on. Requests are now routed to wherever authority genuinely lies.
Fixed an issue where a strip of the landing pad at Orison had no collision

The doorways on the exterior lobby sections had no collision backing them on one side, so at the boundary between the interior and exterior physics grids there was a gap with nothing solid underneath. Invisible collision has been added to both sides of that transition. Creatures
Fixed an issue where removing a Yormandi's eye would leave the empty socket missing its red coloring
Fixed an issue where a freight elevator loading platform could snap into a raised position with cargo still on it while the doors remained closed

Three separate problems were leaving the platform in a state that did not match reality: requests with nothing to move were still being processed, the recovery path could return items it was never meant to, and a closed platform was streaming back in using its raised position. All three have been corrected, so a platform now comes back matching the state it was actually left in.
Resolved an issue where players could not submit cargo for several Orison Relief Support missions at once from the same freight elevator

Two things were going wrong on the same submission path, the count of items a mission order still needed was not being tallied correctly, and stowed cargo was not checking whether an order had already been satisfied. Both have been corrected, so the elevator can now resolve several mission orders in one go instead of stalling after the first.
Fixed an issue where carryable items lost their carry prompt once placed on a cargo grid, leaving them stuck in place
Fixed an issue where equipping a gimbal mount to the Origin X1 series would leave the attached weapon unable to fire or move

The weapon hardpoint was described as holding a weapon directly, with no provision for a gimbal in between, and the pilot seat's control rules only covered a weapon mounted straight onto it. Fitting a gimbal put the weapon one step further out than the ship expected, leaving nothing for the pilot to aim or fire. The hardpoint now describes the gimbal with the weapon nested inside, and the seat's control rules cover that arrangement.
Resolved an issue where a vehicle could become unresponsive after quantum travel on a poor connection

On a poor connection the messages that close out quantum travel could arrive late or out of order, leaving the drive stuck part way through its shutdown with the thrusters never handed back. The end of travel sequence now handles that case, so control returns to the ship even when traffic arrives out of order.
Fixed an issue where shields configured with a flat damage resistance applied no resistance at all

A resistance band was only treated as valid when its minimum sat strictly below its maximum, so any shield whose resistance was set as a single flat figure failed that check and was discarded entirely. The restriction has been removed, and a flat resistance now applies as intended.
Resolved an issue where lowering the rear ramp on all Drake Cutlass variants would raise the vehicle, preventing players from climbing in through the side doors

The rear ramp's collision geometry and surface settings meant that lowering it pushed against the ship instead of swinging clear, levering the whole vehicle upward on its landing gear. With the hull sitting higher than intended, the side doors were out of reach of the climb in animation. The ramp's collision setup and material settings have been corrected so deploying it no longer moves the ship.
Fixed a case where the treads on ground vehicles did not move as the vehicle drove

Tread movement is produced by applying a scrolling material to the tread surface, but a default material had been added to the part above it, and the outer assignment takes precedence over the one the tread system applies. That conflict has been resolved so the tread system's material is the one that actually takes effect, and the treads move with the vehicle again.
Fixed an issue where the radar display on the Mirai Pulse and Pulse LX was inverted
Corrected an issue where the Lephari radar was listed as Grade A instead of Grade C in the mobiGlas Vehicle Loadout Manager
Fixed an issue where hovering over component icons on the power management MFD displayed no name or temperature label
Corrected an issue where some ship components displayed no manufacturer logo
Resolved an issue where equipment worn by a player could deal fatal collision damage to a snub fighter docked to their ship

Magazines on a weapon carried by the player were left without a physics parent, so while the player sat in a seat the game treated them as loose objects moving at the ship's speed. A snub docked to that ship could then be struck by them at full relative velocity. Carried magazines now stay parented to the player.
Fixed a case where the MISC Prospector could come out tilted when retrieved from a hangar

Not all of the Prospector's landing gear mounting points sat at the same height, so the ship could settle unevenly as it was lowered onto the pad and tip to one side. The mounting points have been levelled with one another. It only happened some of the time, which is part of why it went unresolved for so long.
Fixed an issue where a vehicle's engines were already running when it was retrieved from a hangar

A stored ship's power state was not being reapplied when it was placed back on the pad, so it came back powered regardless of how it was left. Power assignment on retrieval has been corrected, so a ship now arrives in the state it was stored in.
Fixed an issue where spawning a Drake Caterpillar with a crew manifest would leave the pilot seat empty

The Caterpillar is flown from a detachable command module, which the game handles as a separate craft docked to the hull, and the crew manifest spawn path had no support for placing an AI pilot inside a docked sub craft, so the seat was simply left empty. Spawning now creates the host ship and its attached module together as a pair and tracks the link between them per vehicle instead of per seat, so manifest crew end up in the module's pilot seat as intended.
Resolved an issue where abandoned vehicles at some stations were not being cleaned up over time, preventing other players from landing

Everus Harbor, Seraphim Station, Bajini Point and Port Tressler were missing the lifetime setting that tells the cleanup pass when a vehicle left sitting at a station should be removed, so nothing parked there ever aged out and pads slowly filled with derelicts. Lifetime overrides have been added for those four stations and exported for the planets they orbit, so abandoned vehicles there are now cleared on a timer like everywhere else.
Corrected an issue where the rear landing gear on all MISC Hull variants appeared pixelated while deploying or retracting

The landing gear animates on its own skeleton attached to the ship, but the motion data it handed the renderer accounted only for its own animation and the ship's position, not the offset between the two from the previous frame. The renderer was therefore told the gear had moved somewhere it had not, which smeared the image while the gear travelled. That offset is now included.
Fixed an issue where both the left and right landing gear on the Kruger Stingray appeared pixelated while retracting or deploying
Fixed an issue where the Aegis Eclipse's landing gear appeared pixelated when retracted or deployed
Fixed an issue where the Aegis Gladius Dunlevy was missing its decals on the rudders and rear wings when retrieved
Corrected an issue where the decals on physicalized storage containers aboard ships disappeared at relatively short distances
Resolved an issue where vehicle modules purchased with aUEC were missing collision and caused parts of the interior to render incorrectly

Modules were being attached as geometry hung off the vehicle's skeleton rather than as objects in their own right, so the module's collision and its interior visibility setup never travelled with it. Modules are now attached as full entities, which brings both along.
Resolved an issue where some weapon racks in ship captain's quarters and armories appeared as placeholder objects and could not be interacted with
Corrected an issue where the bathroom door in ship habitation areas would abruptly change detail when viewed from a distance
Fixed a problem where dropping a stowed heavy machine gun would place it nose down and could cause it to fall through the ground and disappear

Dropping an item from a held or stowed slot released it from a fixed starting position that took no account of how large the item was. For something as long as a heavy machine gun that meant the weapon appeared pivoted nose down and already partly inside the floor, and in some places the physics system resolved that overlap by pushing it all the way through. Dropped items now work out their starting height from their own dimensions.
Corrected an issue where the word \"Barrel\" was missing from the attachment description of the Demeco \"Streamline\" LMG
Corrected an issue where exploration suits displayed four consumable leg slots but only two of them could be used

The suit's leg consumable ports are set up in pairs, and the second port in each pair had not been configured to accept consumables the way the first one was, so the slot was drawn but nothing could go into it. Both of those ports now accept consumables like their counterparts, which makes all four slots usable.
Fixed a case where the Monolith Backpack and its variants had no storage capacity

The backpack was inheriting its properties from the wrong template, one that defines no storage volume at all, so the pack arrived with no inventory space. It now inherits from the correct heavy backpack template and carries its intended capacity.

units.t: Fixed by Hotfix Since 4.10.0 Went Live
n: The following 26 fixes reached the live environment a hotfixes in the weeks after 4.10.0 launched.
Fixed a server crash caused by a mission prop sitting in a player's inventory, which could hold a shard in a repeating crash loop for over an hour
Resolved a server crash where the same object could be queued for cleanup twice and deleted twice
Fixed a server crash while looking up a component that had already been released
Resolved a server crash when a ship's thruster was asked for its capacity while its flight system was being torn down
Fixed memory corruption caused by several parts of the game reading a weapon's fire modes at the same time as they were being cleared
Fixed a crash in the physics system when moving through areas exported before a newer collision check existed
Added a limit on how many loose items can be unstowed onto a freight elevator platform at once, which was capable of chain crashing a server
Resolved an issue where entering a vehicle could overwrite the previous driver without clearing them first, putting the client and server out of step
Fixed a family of issues where a server node would shut down immediately and disconnect everyone on it

The server was accepting a confirmation that an object's layout was final without checking that the layout it had actually matched the one being confirmed. When they disagreed, the node exited rather than continuing. It now verifies the layout first. This covered several separate reports, including repeating shutdowns around the Nyx points of interest and a bad variable index on the ARGO MOLE's turrets.
Fixed a client crash in the graphics layer where a texture view could still be in use while it was being discarded, which surfaced after memory defragmentation was introduced
Resolved an issue where the audio thread could cause significant frame rate drops, and a related audio crash
Improved memory handling for the system that partitions the world into regions, which was allocating and freeing far too often
Restored optimization on a number of files where it had been accidentally left disabled
Fixed an issue where Battaglia's second and third story contracts were never created on busy shards, leaving players with no follow-up after the first

Mission generation was querying locations using stored identifiers that are not valid on every shard, and the caches backing those queries were not being cleared properly when a shard started up. Missions that depended on a Moraine base as their location were the most visible casualty.
Resolved an issue where the Nine Tails commander in Siege of Orison could take collision damage while being teleported between phases, and die instantly
Fixed an issue where a vehicle with an expired idle timer was impounded again within seconds of every retrieval
Fixed an issue where Super Heavy armor could not be unequipped to local inventory if anything was attached to it
Resolved an issue where the mech style footstep audio from the Super Heavy suit kept playing after the armor was unequipped
Fixed an issue where arrow key and gamepad D-pad navigation stopped working in mobiGlas, because a mouse position update sent every frame was clearing the keyboard focus one frame after each press
Fixed an issue where holograms could render incorrectly from certain angles when upscaling was enabled
Resolved several water issues, including simulation not running on ships and broken shading on water volumes and rivers

n: Time again for another Hotfix Central thread to keep you all up to date on things going on outside of the normal patch cycle in SC Alpha 4.10.3 LIVE!
This will be a living document of all the hotfixes applied to the current LIVE environment, along with dates as a timeline and when the HOTFIX channel is open and closed.
This client hotfix has now moved to the LIVE channel with fixes for the top 3 client crashes including the #1 Vulkan crash.

This DGS side hotfix contains multiple server crash fixes along with a fix for the RSI Discovery Event total score is not adding up correctly

This client side hotfix helps with one of the top client crashes happening with Vulkan on the latest Nvidia drivers.
