Today's hotfix in testing covers client, server, and service updates and fixes including:
Client: D-pad navigation fix (should help with macros/voice attack)
Server: Fix for vehicles with an expired idle timer impounding again seconds after retrieval
Server: Mendo Ren sliding off railing in SoO
Service: Fixes for Story 2 and 3 Battaglia contracts not creating properly
Client Side Fix for Super Heavy Combat Armor Sound Effects Playing after Unequiping
Hybrid Side updates for multiple top crashes will be rolling out over time tonight and throughout the weekend to help with the most hit stability issues.
8.27.2026: Hotfix 12535871 is now on the HOTFIX channel and select shards on LIVE

This client and server hotfix for the LIVE environment includes fixes for audio thread framerate issues (linux), water shading and buffer issues with ships, upscaling issues for holographics, super heavy armor cannot be unequipped to local inventory, Mendo Ren falling off the balcony during encounter as well as taking damage from the world and dying randomly after teleport, and further client and server crash and stability fixes.
Teams also have ongoing investigations for the current long interaction delays with many systems in the game and we will update once we have more news.

The HOTFIX channel will become available for periods of time when the client-side of the game needs the hotfix. This channel will point to the LIVE environment and using this will retain and add progress to your LIVE account as if you were playing normally.

The best way to play on the HOTFIX channel, when one is available, is to rename your LIVE folder to HOTFIX and verify using the HOTFIX channel on the launcher. Reverse this process to go back to LIVE once it is released or you would like to stop using this channel.

This will be a living document of all the hotfixes applied to the current LIVE environment, along with dates as a timeline and when the HOTFIX channel is open and closed.

patches.title: Star Citizen Alpha 4.9 LIVE Release Notes

n: Star Citizen Alpha 4.9 has been released onto the LIVE environment!
Your launcher should now display: VERSION 4.9.0-LIVE.12232306
Reminder. Citizens always imprint their ship loadouts before adventuring into the universe!

units.t: New Missions: Supporting Recco Battaglia Contracts
n: Implementing a new set of repeatable missions from Recco Battaglia, an independent mining logistics coordinator based in Levski. Take on a variety of contracts including prospecting, mining, recovery, salvage, investigations, ship reclamation, and more, while building your reputation with Recco to unlock additional opportunities in Alpha 4.9 and beyond. Contracts can be accepted through your mobiGlas.

Mission reputation rewards include exclusive blueprints for People's Alliance armor pieces and Klescher Laser Repeater weapon components as well as unique variants of the Drake Golem, MISC Prospector, and Argo MOLE delivered to your home location at higher reputation tiers.

Missiles and torpedoes placed on a cargo grid will now display a bounding box frame around them, making it easy to adjust placement, stack, and see the footprint each piece of ordnance occupies. The frame is visible anywhere a cargo grid appears, including ship interiors and freight elevators. When snapping ordnance into position, both the missile/torp and its frame are now shown in the hologram placement preview, and players can choose which direction the ordnance snaps before confirming placement.

The Local and External toggle buttons in the Freight Elevator Kiosk have been replaced with a single \"Show External\" checkbox, making it easier to switch between viewing items stored locally in your hangar and items stored in external warehouses.

The Claim button now displays a tooltip when it cannot be used, explaining the reason. Possible states include insufficient funds, too many items selected, items currently on cooldown, or no items selected.

The message displayed when a cargo transfer only partially completes has been updated to more clearly communicate what happened. When the elevator platform cannot accommodate all selected items, it will transfer as many as it can fit and leave the remainder in the warehouse. The updated message now reflects this, and the button to dismiss the popup now correctly closes it.

With the addition of armor on ships into the game, we have rebalanced the entire ship roster for missions and are working on going through all combat missions and making adjustments and tweaks. No more Industrial ships should spawn in combat missions unless explicitly told to spawn. Rebalanced all the Defend Ship missions to spawn a lower class attacker on the ship to defend to give players more of a fair opportunity to save the ships

Experimental Scanning Updates have been put into 4.9 that will allow easier scanning of materials throughout the PU. We will be monitoring LIVE to make sure this update isn't having any negative effects on stability.
Ship mining laser power has been increased across the board by about 20%
Added Behring CQ7 Bullpup Rifle and ammo to shops across multiple locations
Tractor beams can now be used inside armistice zones at Distribution Centers
Ship Attenuation and Flyby Audio playback rules adjusted across all ships for better audio falloff at range along with flyby audio mix polish
Grenade HUD Markers: Live grenades will now display a warning marker on the HUD
Bombing Run Missions: Bombing Run missions are now regional and will only appear in the area of space where the mission takes place, rather than being visible system-wide
Named waypoints added to key locations across Nyx
Nyx Resource Distribution: Common resource distribution adjusted at Glacium and Keeger HPP locations in Nyx
Destroy Satellite Missions: Missions are now regional, preventing players from seeing and accepting satellite missions across all of Stanton
Salvage mission unlock chain implemented for Adagio paid salvage contracts
Commodity kiosks removed from Dumper's Depot and Platinum Bay and replaced with item kiosks.
Jump drives added to Dumper's Depot Area18 shelving
Food and drink added to Dumper's Depot inventory
Additional shop kiosks added to New Deal ship dealership in Lorville

Ships now provide visual and audio feedback on your reticle each time a shot connects, telling you exactly what your weapons are doing to a target in real time. Previously, ship combat provided no meaningful feedback on how shots were having an effect. Hit markers now change state based on the result of each shot, with a distinct audio cue for each outcome.
No Damage / Deflected: your shot reached the target but was deflected by the armor and dealt no damage
Shield Hit: your shot connected with an active shield
Armor Hit: your shot damaged the armor layer
Hull Hit: your shot reached the hull, either by penetrating through armor or because the armor was already depleted
Component Hit: your shot struck an internal component such as a power plant, cooler, or weapon
Component Destroyed: your shot destroyed an internal component

Each hit marker state is accompanied by a distinct audio cue, allowing pilots to assess shot results by ear without watching the reticle closely. After director feedback, the initial six-layer audio palette was refined down to three core layers for clarity: Armor Hit, Component Hit, and Component Destroyed. The hit marker audio has been fully decoupled from the legacy Ships Computer audio system and replaced with a new, higher-fidelity sound palette built specifically for combat feedback.
We have done a balance pass on Ballistic Repeater weapons to greatly reduce their damage.
BEHR Ballistic Cannon S4: damage increased from 325 to 1090 physical per shot. armor penetration distance reduced, and fire rate delay increased.
BEHR Ballistic Gatling S5: damage reduced from 126.5 to 102.5 physical per shot
Esperia Deadbolt Cannon S4: damage reduced from 683.1 to 610 physical per shot
Esperia Deadbolt Cannon S5: damage reduced from 1024.2 to 950 physical per shot
Vanduul Plasma Cannon S5: damage reduced from 1000 to 970 energy per shot
Vanduul shields updated with improved glow and hexagon visual effects
Capital ships can now access hangar services when any portion of the ship overlaps a servicing zone, rather than requiring the ship's center pivot point to be fully inside the zone.
Implementing two new hairstyles, along with an update to one hairstyle to bring it up to current quality standards.

units.t: Juvenile and Adult Valakkar Behavior Updates
n: Updates to Valakar behaviors have been made to further distinguish types as well as fix issues previously encountered. Sentry Valakkars will not Bite and will instead hide if you get too close. Mobile Valakkars will move in combat to chase you down or reposition. Juvenile Valakkars now have a Bite Attack. Ensured that Valakkars always have a purpose in being above ground (reduces idle wiggling). Fixed bugs with some Valakkar attacks not doing damage.

units.t: New FPS Weapon: Behring \"CQ7\" Bullpup Rifle
n: Design Notes from Zac: After a year of very interesting sci-fi weapons (and some very rusty ones), we heard a lot of feedback of wanting a nice standard lower RPM rifle to be added into the mix. So what better missing 'standard' than a bullpup? that and the amount of times I got sent the old concept art for the behring bullpup on spectrum over my time working here, I knew it had to be this.

To make this stand out this weapon has a nice sharp TTK for a rifle but having a consistent and followable Y recoil shaped pattern, to those who learn it will be able to consistent land shots on target, Behring weapons typically always have very consistent and readable recoil and this weapon is no different, having a bit of 'bite' to its power but still in the 'feels smooth to use' that you expect from behring. Overall this is a great, all rounder daily driver type of rifle that won't let you down.
The weapon can be found in Ship In Distress missions as well as Moraine Data Retrieval and Moraine Movements both take you to the base where you can find the QB7.

units.t: New FPS Clothing: Bellator Combat Suit
n: A new tailored civilian suit is now available in the Persistent Universe, inspired by the refined but dangerous look of high-end professional clothing. Despite its formal appearance, the suit consisting of a jacket, trousers, dress shirt, and shoes, provides a small degree of damage mitigation and weapon attachments not found in standard civilian clothing, making it a practical choice for players who want to blend in without going completely unprotected.

The jacket features 2 magazine slots and 1 stocked weapon slot. The stocked weapon remains visible on the outside of the jacket at all times. A sidearm and knife can each be carried concealed, becoming hidden when the matching jacket is worn. The trousers include 2 medpen slots and a knife slot.

Ship flyby audio has been overhauled in 4.9.0. The audio that plays when a ship passes near you or another vessel is now driven by a new procedural system that triggers consistently and with better audio attenuation, addressing a long-standing issue where flyby sounds would fail to play or fall silent.
Stereo cursor is now fully body-aligned and no longer shifts position when affected by external forces such as water, elevators, or trains
Fixed stereo cursor being invisible when hovering over radar UI elements
Fixed a performance issue caused by an optimization that was submitted in a previous PTU build

Added updated cleanup code for abandoned ships around locations in the PU. This new code adds ship cleanup rules that will cleanup ships in an abandoned state after 5 hours to better reduce ship clutter around high impact locations. This code will affect all major landing zones and space stations in Stanton and Nyx, as well as Grim Hex, Levski, and other social stations across Nyx.

Updates to ASOP terminal code to help ships that are currently spawning in transit to a pad to now correctly suppress the claim button, preventing a false claimable state during delivery. Further update have also been done to make it so the terminal can now correctly query vehicles stored in hangar inventory, preventing incorrect \"Claim only\" status on stored ships

units.t: New Mission: Defend Location - Ship Battles V3
units.c: New Mission: Defend Location - Ship Battles V3
n: Ship Battles V3 introduces the Defend Location archetype, a style of ship combat mission that has been a design goal since the original Ship Battles release. The premise is straightforward: a location is under attack and it is your job to stop it. Enemy bombers make coordinated strafing runs on fuel storage and other critical infrastructure, and your task is to intercept them before they can complete those runs. Let too many get through and the mission fails.

Alongside the core Defend mission, V3 also introduces a combined archetype that layers an escort objective on top of the defense. While you are shooting down bombers, a friendly ship is either launching from the station or inbound for landing, and hostile fighters are focusing on it. Both objectives are active at the same time. Completing both is required to succeed, and failing either ends the mission. This combined variant is the more demanding of the two and is designed to stress different ship classes, with interceptors and heavier fighters filling different parts of the engagement.

V3 also updates the existing Escort Ship archetype from V2 with Ace Pilot spawns and more varied escort ship flight paths, increasing the difficulty ceiling and reducing the predictability of those missions for players who have already run them extensively. Defend Location missions are available across asteroid mining bases in Stanton, Pyro, and Nyx at a wide range of difficulty tiers.

Tactical Strike Group is a new endgame verified mercenary contract designed for large, organized player squads. The mission tasks players with assaulting a fortified Nyx asteroid base held by hostile forces (QV Extraction Stations), working through a six-phase assault that demands tight coordination across ship classes and combat roles. The contract scales in intensity as each phase of the station is dismantled. The rewards will be great expect heavy resistance throughout.

Rally the strike force and escort the People's Alliance Idris Tranquility into position. The Idris will serve as your mobile rearm, repair, and refuel platform throughout the engagement. Establish perimeter defense before pushing on the station.

Target the station's external Power Relays with ballistic weapons — energy weapons are ineffective against hardened station targets. Destroying all relays opens access to the superstructure trench runs.
Cooling Units are vulnerable to energy weapons. Smaller ships must navigate the internal superstructure trenches to reach them, accumulating Distortion Damage the longer they remain inside.
// 04 - Destroy the Core and Defend Tranquility

Breach the core chamber once the shutters open. Distortion and radiation intensity increases dramatically inside. Simultaneously, hostile forces will escalate attacks on Tranquility so exterior ships must maintain its defense.
With the core destroyed the station's interior FPS section becomes accessible. A ground team boards and fights through the station to reach the override terminal.
Extract hostage pilot Gabe Windell from Shattered Blade custody and get him safely off the station to complete the contract.
Available via Contract Manager in Nyx under Verified Mercenary Contracts
Designed for squads of 7 or more ships across multiple sizes and classes
Smaller ships are required to navigate the station's internal superstructure trenches
Larger ships support exterior combat and defend Tranquility throughout all phases
The People's Alliance Idris, Tranquility, provides on-site repair, rearm, and refuel for ships that fit in its hangar

Trench run entrances unlock when all Power Relays are destroyed; the FPS interior opens once the Core is down

One of many kinds of stations abandoned across the Nyx system by QV Planetary Services, the QV Extraction Stations were once functional industrial operations left behind as the company cut its losses in the region. They have since found volatile new life as fortified strongholds. Derelict arms and corroded superstructure surround a hardened interior that now houses the faction's operations, and serves as the battleground for the Tactical Strike Group contract.

What you wear in the cockpit now has a direct effect on how well your body handles the forces of high-performance flight. Flight suits are purpose-built for this environment and improve your g-force tolerance above the unequipped baseline, letting you sustain tighter maneuvers longer before blacking out. Combat armor works in the opposite direction: it is built for ground engagements and protection, not for sustained high-g flight, and will reduce your g-force tolerance accordingly. This change makes loadout decisions more meaningful for pilots and creates a clearer distinction between gear designed for flying and gear designed for fighting.

Many of the flight suits can be purchased with aUEC in game at locations such as Cubby Blast in Area18, Tammany and Sons in Lorville, Cordry's in Levski, Skutters in Grim HEX, and indy tradeposts in Pyro.
G-force tolerance is now dynamically calculated based on the clothing and armor worn by the player
Flight suits provide a positive g-force resistance modifier, improving your tolerance above the unequipped baseline
Combat armor applies a negative modifier, reducing g-force tolerance that increases in increments based on light, medium, heavy types and compared to flying unequipped
Undersuits also contribute to the total g-force resistance calculation and are factored into the final value
The modifier is distributed across the full armor set, so partial loadouts result in proportionally adjusted tolerance
Combat flight suits now provide 15% damage mitigation in addition to their g-force resistance bonus, giving pilots a defensive trade-off when choosing flight gear over combat armor
Arena Commander race modes now spawn players in the best available racing flight suit by default, ensuring competitive events start with optimal g-force configuration
Higher Tolerances: Racing or Combat Flight Suit

Dedicated flight suits are optimized for high-g environments and provide the highest g-force tolerance available. Racing suits are tuned for sustained performance in competition; combat flight suits offer meaningful resistance alongside 15% damage mitigation.

Flying without any armor or suit is the reference point for g-force tolerance. All modifiers are applied relative to this state. A player with no worn items experiences the default g-force resistance.
Reduced: Light or Medium Combat Armor

Lighter combat armor loadouts apply a moderate negative modifier to g-force tolerance. Pilots wearing partial or light armor sets will notice reduced resistance compared to flying unequipped, but the impact is less severe than full heavy armor.
Greatly Reduced: Full Heavy Combat Armor

A complete heavy armor loadout represents the lowest g-force tolerance in the system. Heavy armor provides maximum damage protection for ground combat but significantly reduces your ability to sustain high-g maneuvers in a cockpit. Plan your loadout accordingly.

Refueling content in 4.8 comes in multiple parts with new Refueling missions as well as Improvements to the overall refueling playability. The first is a new set of contracts from the United Wayfarers Club that give players who own refueling ships a dedicated mission type to engage with. The second part is a significant overhaul to how ship-to-ship refueling works at the system level, making the process faster, clearer, and less punishing.

With this update, there is a new operator mode on the refuelling ship to enable Refueling operator mode, just like salvage or mining mode. Players can enter the mode by pressing “M”. Entering the mode will automatically extend/retract the fuel nozzle allowing either party to send requests for docking to initiate the refueling process. Once docked, fuel transfer can be initiated through the Vehicle Maintenance App, just select the amount, confirm the purchase, and the fuel moves. For the fuel giver it changed however: As long as there are relevant pods open, the fuel flows automatically as soon as a purchase was made. Players can still manually control the flow: opening/closing pods and transfer fuel from one pod to another. Ten new fuel pods and nozzles are also being added, along with refueling beacons that let players in need of fuel broadcast a request to anyone in the area.
Refueling contracts are now available from the United Wayfarers Club via the Contract Manager
Contracts are specifically designed for pilots operating refueling ships such as the Starfarer
Payment is held in escrow during the refueling process and released on successful completion
AI ships involved in contracts are always passive and will never initiate docking; the player must send the docking request
There are Multi Ship Refuel missions where more than one ship in a given area is out of fuel and the player is sent to refuel them all

Refueling Beacon (For Ships Out of Fuel)
Players who have run out of fuel can now submit a refueling beacon from their MobiGlas, specifying whether they need Hydrogen, Quantum Fuel, or both
Within a short period, an AI Starfarer will respond to the beacon and fly out to assist
A ship that is completely out of fuel cannot move, but autodocking does not require fuel, so the stranded player can still complete the connection

A ship has run out of fuel and is stationary at the marked location. Fly out, extend your refueling boom, dock to the vessel, and fill its tanks to complete the contract. The stranded AI ship will accept your docking request and QT away once refueled. Best suited for Starfarer-class ships with sufficient fuel pod capacity to fill a target tank from empty.
Receive Fuel from an AI Refueler Contract

An AI Starfarer will quantum travel to your position and offer to refuel your ship. Target the AI ship, press N to request docking, align to their nozzle, and confirm your fuel purchase in the Vehicle Maintenance App. Payment is taken from escrow once fuel transfer is complete and you undock. The AI ship will QT away after the exchange.

Not every distress beacon is genuine. Some contracts will lead you to a decoy satellite broadcasting a fake fuel request signal. Upon arrival, the mission provider will warn you something is wrong before hostile AI ships quantum in and attack. Eliminating the attackers earns a bonus reward above the base contract payout. Running from the engagement still completes the contract for the base amount. Hostile ship count is kept low given you will be flying a refueling vessel.
Docking, Fuel Transfer, and New Items
Flow speed is now a fixed property of the nozzle and cannot be manually adjusted. Nozzles can no longer be damaged by incorrect flow speed settings
Hydrogen fuel is always delivered before Quantum Fuel when both are requested. Pods for both types can be opened at the same time without manual switching
10 new items are being added: 5 new fuel pods and 5 new nozzles, with existing items rebalanced. Pods and nozzles vary in flow speed, storage capacity, and damage resistance
Refueling pods have all had a large increase in how much fuel they can hold
Stats on the fuel nozzle and pods received a rework: Pods now add a modifier on the flow speed that is defined by the nozzle. And we have separate flow speed for QUA and HDY fuel
Refueling pods are now available for purchase at stations via the commodity shop
The pod management interface has been consolidated from two screens into one
Pod fill amounts are now displayed as a current/total value (for example, 450/600 SCU) rather than as a percentage
Valve control elements have been removed from the pod management screen
Payment information, process timeline, and an Abort button remain on screen during active refueling
A control hint for entering Refueling Mode now appears in the lower right of the HUD when seated in the pilot seat

Item Recovery for vehicles changes how ship claims work at a fundamental level. Previously, claiming a ship always returned the manufacturer default configuration, and any modifications you had made to it were simply gone. With this update, you can now save a snapshot of your ship's current loadout at the ASOP terminal. When your ship is destroyed and you file a claim, you will have a choice: claim the manufacturer default for free with a longer cooldown, or claim your saved insured loadout at an aUEC cost with a shorter cooldown. Your custom components and weapons can all be preserved through claims as long as you kept a snapshot up to date.
It is very important to remember to imprint your loadout before leaving the hangar!

Along with this update we have made other adjustments to the ASOP which include a limit of 25 ships delivered per location and a new Local ships only view to make sure you can quickly see what you have delivered. On the local ship view, you will be able to destroy a ship when needed.

A record of your ship's current loadout saved at the ASOP terminal. Includes equipped components, ship weapons, locker contents, and poster decorations attached to wall slots. Ammo and missiles are excluded. Bricked items cannot be included.
An item that has been included in a snapshot and can be claimed back if lost.
A claim that returns your ship in the state it was when you last took a snapshot. Costs aUEC based on the hull and the value of the saved configuration. Does not include ammo or missiles.
When a registered item is claimed, the original copy enters a bricked state after a brief grace period and becomes non-functional. Bricked ships and items remain in your hangar and can be scrapped.
When filing a claim after a ship is destroyed, you now have two options at the ASOP terminal: claim the manufacturer loadout or claim your saved insured loadout
The manufacturer loadout claim is free and uses the default configuration from your RSI web hangar or the in-game default. It has a longer cooldown timer
The insured loadout claim returns your ship with all registered components and equipment in place. It costs aUEC based on the components saved to the loadout and has a shorter cooldown
Cooldown timers for insured claims begin when you spawn the ship, not when it is destroyed
The option to pay aUEC to reduce a standard claim timer has been removed as this is now part of the insured loadout
Ships claimed in either mode will brick any previously active copy of the same ship after a short grace period
Use the save icon on the ASOP terminal while your ship is retrieved to snapshot its current loadout
Snapshots include the ship's equipped components, weapons, and placed poster decorations
Taking a new snapshot replaces the previous one. Items no longer in the new snapshot lose their registered status unless they appear in another vehicle's snapshot

Nested vehicles (such as a fighter stored inside a larger ship) are included in the parent ship's snapshot if present when the snapshot is taken. Nested ships can also have their own independent snapshots
Stolen AI ships cannot be registered or included in a snapshot
A single registered item can appear in snapshots for multiple ships simultaneously
Ammo and missiles are consumables and are not returned when claiming an insured loadout. You must restock and rearm via ship services after each claim
Fuses are restored to the state they were in when the snapshot was saved
Bricked ships are not automatically removed from hangar storage. You can call them up in your hangar to retrieve any cargo that was aboard before scrapping them
You can scrap a bricked ship from your hangar. Scrapped ships you own can still be claimed back later

The Vehicle Manager App (VMA) no longer saves ship loadouts. Saving a loadout must now be done through the ASOP terminal

units.t: New Ship: Drake Ironclad & Ironclad Assault
n: The Drake Ironclad lineup has now been introduced into the PU. These large logistics and combat platform ships are build around the use of Drake's Command Modules. Unlike conventional ships, the Ironclad cannot be piloted on its own. The included Drake Command Module must be docked and paired with the hull before flight control is available.

The Command Module feature introduces a new ship pairing mechanic where a smaller, fully pilotable command ship takes control of a larger host ship that cannot fly on its own. For this 4.8.0 PTU, this applies to the Drake Caterpillar. Without a Command Module attached, the host Caterpillar cannot be piloted.

The core flow is: The Parasite docks to the Host and initiates a System Migration Procedure (SMP), a brief transitional phase during which both ships are non-functional, after which the Parasite's pilot gains full control of the paired unit through the Host's systems. The process reverses cleanly on undocking.

Default docking has been moved to a new keybind to avoid collision with landing gear toggle: RALT+N for Ship-to-ship docking/undocking (preferred over ALT+N to keep ATC requests on tap ALT+N and for HOTAS usability).
The SMP is implemented as a new mode so it can apply ship-wide changes across UI, audio, and VFX simultaneously to both vehicles.
All MFDs on both the Parasite and the Host display a dedicated transfer UI showing migration progress
No thrusters or weapons are operable on either ship
The command module cannot undock during this phase
Cockpit lights on the command module change color to indicate the transition state

After SMP completes movement input controls both ships as a single unit. The Power Management MFD controls the Host's power allocation. Self-Status MFD and MFD Casts display the combined Command Module and Host instead of just the command module. All standard vehicle functionality is available: combat, QT, landing services, docking to ships and stations.

The Aegis Hammerhead has received its Gold Standard pass, bringing the ship's interior up to the level of quality established by more recently built and reworked vessels. Every area of the interior has been reviewed and polished from the crew quarters and cargo hold through to the turret cockpits, the captain's quarters, and the service areas below decks. The update also addresses a significant number of functional issues that have been present in the ship since its original release, including missing collision on several interior geometry pieces, visarea and atmosphere problems in the turrets, overloaded life support, and a collection of interaction and UI fixes across the cargo elevator, component bays, and power relay systems.

Capital Ship Hangar Service brings the same repair, restock, and refuel services you use at landing zones directly onto large capital ships. When landed in the hangar of a supporting vessel, you can open your MobiGlas and request ship services just as you would at any station or outpost. This first release makes the feature available on the AI Idris in the Tactical Strike Groups mission as well as some of the current larger ships.

With this update, players will be able to use their Idris, Polaris, and 890j to refuel ships that are fully able to land in their hangars while some ships such as the 600i explorer and Carrack are meant to be able to restock ground vehicles that fit.
Land in the hangar of a ship that offers servicing and remain seated in your ship
Open your MobiGlas and navigate to the Vehicle Maintenance Services app, the same interface used at landing zones and stations
Request repair, restock, or refuel as needed; multiple ships can be serviced simultaneously
Services do not require any action from the crew of the ship

units.t: New FPS Weapon: Kastak Arms - Plasma Grenade
n: Implementing Kastak Arms area-denial grenade. Prime and throw to lock down an area and prevent enemies from pushing through.

The Kastak Arms Plasma Grenade is the first area-denial grenade in Star Citizen. Unlike fragmentation grenades that deliver a single explosion, the Plasma Grenade detonates repeatedly after landing, unleashing a sustained series of plasma bursts that make the affected zone extremely dangerous to push through. It is designed to hold positions, flush enemies out of cover, and punish opponents who try to advance through a doorway or corridor. Prime it, throw it, and let the grenade do the work.
Detonates repeatedly after landing, producing a sustained zone of plasma explosions for several seconds
Deals Energy (Plasma) damage with each detonation within a 15-meter effective radius
Has no arming time and begins its detonation sequence on a timed fuse after being thrown
Can be shot mid-flight to trigger early detonation before it reaches the intended landing point
Designed to deny movement through a zone rather than deliver a single high-damage burst
Most effective in chokepoints, doorways, corridors, and any area where enemies must pass through to advance
Coordinate with teammates to force enemies into the denial zone rather than letting them wait it out in cover
The grenade can be intercepted and detonated early by enemy fire, so time your throw carefully in contested space
Available for purchase at weapons vendors and found in the world as loot

This released brings the very first integration of the D-BOX SDK and enable support for their haptic systems. This is the first in what will be a series of updates to our motion telemetry support, and for the time being it is considered experimental.

Star Citizen is a game built around the fantasy of being in the cockpit, and we want the physical experience to match what's on screen or headset. We know our players have been building incredible custom cockpits and simrigs setups of every shape and size, from compact desk rigs, spherical displays, and custom physical cockpits all the way to a literal bus (omg!). We want the game to be able to leverage that hardware to bring you the next level of immersion.

A haptic system is built from motion actuators, which are motor-driven units that mount under your seat or rig. Each actuator can produce two types of output: physical movement (pushing the platform up and down) and haptic rumble, which can range from subtle fine vibrations you barely notice to deep reverberations that move the entire rig.

A basic two-actuator setup gives two degrees of freedom: Roll and Pitch, as well as vibrations and texture. Four-actuator configurations add more range and precision with a third degree of freedom added: Heave.. Higher-end setups running up to eight actuators can support full Sway, Surge and Yaw on top of that. D-BOX is one of the leading manufacturers of these systems, and their technology is what we've integrated with for this release.
We focused this first pass entirely on the cockpit experience. Everything integrated so far is tuned for space and atmospheric flight:
Directional hits (with attenuation based on shields vs. hull damage)
The goal of this integration is to make piloting feel visceral, especially in combat.

You'll feel your ship's engine rumble scale with its size, so a Pisces hums while a Hammerhead growls through your seat. Hitting afterburner or boost gives you a real kickback. Firing weapons produces recoil that matches the output and launching missiles or popping countermeasures each have their own reaction. When something hits your ship, the impact is directional and attenuated based on whether your shields absorbed it or it punched through to hull. A glancing hit against full shields feels very different from a torpedo connecting with bare armor.

Beyond combat, the platform responds to the G-forces your pilot is experiencing, so hard turns, acceleration, and deceleration all translate to physical movement in your seat. Deploying and retracting landing gear has its own tactile signature and switching into decouple mode gives you a distinct engagement feel, so you know the moment your flight model changes. When it all comes together, your body starts reacting before your brain does. That's when you know the immersion is working.

Note that this release is focused on the pilot seat experience. Turret positions have a preliminary pass for weapon fire and movement, but broader multi-crew coverage and FPS/EVA are not covered yet and are on our radar for future updates.

If you have a D-BOX system, install the motion code for Star Citizen and it will automatically detect the haptic system and start processing telemetry. The platform should initialize its up/down cycle. That's it.
You can grab the motion code by accessing D-BOX HaptiSync Center. There is no need to configure anything on your game client to activate the integration.
